analysis.title: Asia Open - Awaiting America's verdict
key_insights: US midterm election day: all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are up. Democrats are widely expected to retake the House and are slight favorites for the Senate, within the margin of error. Market attention is on the Senate.
A Dem sweep is increasingly priced in, which Citi says suggests a benign outcome for a divided result.
NDX rose 68bps on a semis-led rebound after positive earnings. The SOX gained 2.6% after results from ETN, FN, LSCC and ON, with more earnings due this week.

USTs sold off 3-5bps across the curve after JOLTS job openings came in well above estimates, largely from manufacturing supported by AI investment and tax incentives that Citi economists see fading in 2027. Focus turns to Wednesday's quarterly refunding announcement at 08:30 EST.

Citi's David Bieber saw new duration longs in the US versus mixed flows in EGBs. Positioning remains structurally short, systematics need larger moves to flip long, and long-end flattener positions remain vulnerable.
CTAs were signaled to flip short SPX after last week's sharp sell-off and are estimated to need to sell $15bn of unlevered SPX e-mini notional this week to reach the new short position.
The equity trading strategy desk is watching Governor's races in TX, OH and GA because of their large data center exposure.

The dollar firmed on the AI-trade rebound and strong US jobs data. USDJPY rose 0.49% to 158.723, the weakest G10 performer was the yen. BRL fell 1%, MXN 1.4% and COP 1.2% after reopening from the holiday.
Citi's G10 options desk reduced USDJPY vol positions in favor of AUDJPY downside expressions.
Crude extended its decline to over 9%, with US-Iran diplomacy and the midterms the near-term focus. Silver (-1.9%) underperformed gold (-0.62%) as central banks keep supporting bullion.

BRL weakened on uncertainty around Lula's cabinet. USDBRL at 5.50 looks stretched ahead of Wednesday's rate decision, where a hold is expected. Ibovespa fell about 1.6% and is 14% lower over the past month.
Riksbank decides at 08:30 GMT. OIS prices about 17bp and the Bloomberg survey leans toward a 25bp hike. Citi tentatively expects a 25bp hike with balanced guidance.

earnings_insights: ETN, FN, LSCC and ON reported constructive results (no figures given), with more earnings due this week. The SOX gained 2.6% on them.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Driven largely by manufacturing, supported by AI investment and tax incentives that Citi economists see fading in 2027. Pushed USTs 3-5bps higher.
Employment change expected at 0.3% vs 0.4% prior, offset by private sector wages at 0.6% vs 0.7% prior.
Core inflation is near the 2% target, so holding is also compelling. Communication on future moves is expected to stay balanced.
Slower disinflation in food and regulated prices offsets more moderate fuel price growth.
Citi does not expect it to be market-moving after the national print.
USDBRL at 5.50 looks stretched ahead of the decision.
